cim: SIU School of Medicine developing AI medical training
cim_eredeti: SIU School of Medicine developing AI medical training
szoveg_eredeti:
Lab builds digital avatars for students to practice difficult patient conversations.

SPRINGFIELD, Ill. (WAND) — The Springfield Memorial Foundation and SIU School of Medicine are investing $2 million to develop medical training programs that use artificial intelligence.adButlerLazyLoad("1318206001881446530",100,["722446","722446","722446"],"177046");

The work is underway at the Ed Curtis Laboratory for Innovation in Medical Education.

The technology allows the team at SIU Medicine to turn real people into avatars and have medical professionals train them on common patient interactions and questions. Medical students can then use a camera and microphone to engage with the avatars.

“The age of AI has really ushered in a remarkable new era of simulation,” said Pinckney Benedict, program director and chief architect for the lab. “Because you can have conversations now without needing another person.”

One of the lab’s primary platforms is a difficult conversations simulator. Benedict said the simulator focuses less on diagnostic material and more on relationships and on learning to give people bad news with empathy.

“As the attending physician in the O.R., you have to go out and tell this family that their grandmother is dying and there is no training for it,” Benedict said. “This training means you’re not doing it cold. It’s not the first time you’ve ever done anything like that.”adButlerLazyLoad("178686337287976011",100,["722446","722446","722446"],"177046");

The program includes training on a variety of situations, including sending a patient to hospice care, educating about a new allergy or delivering a cancer diagnosis.

Benedict said the cases come directly from doctors. He said the lab recently began working with correctional medicine, focusing on medical questions that arise within institutions run by the Illinois Department of Corrections.

Benedict said the lab also built the platform so doctors can create their own cases. A user can type in a description, such as a person with lung cancer, and the platform creates the case.

“We want to be preeminent in the field of digital medical simulation,” said Benedict. “More simulation of human interaction, you know, helping people to learn and practice empathy.”

The lab hopes to share the AI training program with medical schools across the country.adButlerLazyLoad("20144806319830248",100,["722446","722446","722446"],"177046");
